issues.description: The problem statement and tests refer to a function make_y_state(circ, q, p) but the template defines create_y_state(circ, q, p). The solution implements make_y_state. This name/signature mismatch between the template and the specification will block students and automated tests (which expect make_y_state) and cause confusion about which function to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template function create_y_state to make_y_state and ensure its signature matches the specification (make_y_state(circ: stim.Circuit, q: int, p: float) -> None). Alternatively, update the problem statement and tests to refer to create_y_state consistently. Prefer renaming the template to make_y_state to match the problem statement and the provided solution.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to a helper that prepares a noisy |Y> resource state as make_y_state(...), but the template repository defines this stub under the different name create_y_state(...). This naming mismatch will confuse students: the instructions and tests expect make_y_state, while the starter code provides create_y_state, causing students to either implement the wrong identifier or spend time reconciling the mismatch.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the template stub create_y_state(...) to make_y_state(...) (and update any internal references and the NotImplementedError message) so the template, problem statement, and solution use the same identifier. Alternatively, update the problem statement/tests to refer to create_y_state consistently, but prefer aligning the template to the problem's specified name make_y_state.
